title: Torsion-free groups small-doubling abelianity conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a torsion-free group and let $S$ be a finite subset of $G$ satisfying

$$
|S|\geq 3,
$$

and $e\in S$, where $e$ is the identity element of $G$. Write $S^2=\{s_1s_2:s_1,s_2\in S\}$ and let $\langle S\rangle$ denote the subgroup generated by $S$.

**Small-doubling abelianity conjecture.** If

$$
|S^2|\leq 3|S|-3,
$$

then $\langle S\rangle$ is an abelian subgroup of $G$.

The source describes this as a further conjecture believed to be true. It would give a general abelianity criterion for sufficiently small product sets in torsion-free groups, beyond the special decompositions into disjoint abelian sets.
source_name: Mohan and Neetu, “On Small Doubling in Right-Ordered Groups and Baumslag-Solitar Groups-II”, arXiv:2607.11194 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11194

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).
